correctness.rationale: For all real k>1 and all c>=0,L>0, Gamma(k,k) and Exp(1) have a strictly unimodal likelihood ratio with exactly two density intersections alpha<1<beta. Their CDF difference H decreases, increases, decreases and has one unique positive interior zero ell; two strictly decreasing equal-height companion distances classify every finite-window difference H(c+L)-H(c) including its exact boundary signs, uniqueness, simplicity and monotone curves. Concentration and Gamma CLT supply the high-shape quantile limit. Original checker path check_window.py executed 59,007 finite assertions for representative real and integer shapes; numerical tests are not the infinite proof. The physical exit event is carefully separated from settlement.

Reflected density asymmetry and Gaussian central mass involve different functionals; spectral and spatial results involve different state variables. The central new implication requires the two equal-height companion constructions and their strict monotonicity. A generic density crossing lemma alone does not report the complete window-onset phase diagram, though it helps prove it.

value.rationale: This is a mathematically motivated complete decision boundary: matching the mean residence time is insufficient to determine how often model exits occur during a finite competence period. The theorem shows a genuine negative-positive-negative advantage at short windows, proves a unique critical width at which the first switch disappears, tracks both onsets monotonically with window width, and quantifies a large-stage Gaussian limit. Such an exact regime map is more informative than isolated numerical examples or a routine moment calculation; nevertheless it is only a conditional export-timing sensitivity benchmark, not a biological success prediction.
